topic_title: The Skull Britain Wrote a Law to Keep

slides.headline: Africa's Oldest Human Skull Lives in London
slides.body: Kabwe Man is 300,000 years old, found in Zambia. He has spent 105 years locked in a British museum drawer.

slides.headline: A Mine, A Skull, A Shipment
slides.body: 1921: miners at Broken Hill, Northern Rhodesia, struck the skull. The Rhodesia Broken Hill Mine Company shipped it straight to London that same year.

slides.headline: Zambia Asked. Britain Said No.
slides.body: In 1972, Zambia's government formally demanded the skull back, calling it vital to its history. Britain has refused every request since.

slides.headline: The Law Written to Keep It
slides.body: UK deaccession law exempts human remains only if under 1,000 years old. The skull is 300,000. It cannot legally leave.

slides.headline: The Loophole Empire Wrote Itself
slides.body: Colonial law rarely bans return outright. It just defines the terms narrowly enough that nothing taken ever legally qualifies to go home.

slides.headline: Whose Ancestor Gets to Decide?
slides.body: UNESCO ruled for Zambia in 2024. London still has the final say. What would it take to change that?
